---

The official Rust library for the Tungo Platform API (`https://api.tungo.kz`): the AI accountant, 1C integration, bank statements, e-invoices, tax forms and automations of [Tungo AI](https://tungo.kz).

It is generated from the API's OpenAPI contract, so its methods and models always match the contract it was built from.

## Requirements

Rust 1.86 or newer and a [Tokio](https://tokio.rs) runtime with the time driver enabled (`#[tokio::main]` enables it). The client is asynchronous and built on [reqwest](https://docs.rs/reqwest) (TLS through rustls by default), serde and thiserror.

## Installation

Add the crate and a Tokio runtime to `Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[dependencies]
tungo-sdk = "0.3"
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread"] }
```

Cargo features:

| Feature | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rustls-tls` | yes | TLS through rustls |
| `native-tls` | no | TLS through the platform's native library; use it with `default-features = false` |
| `rust_decimal` | no | `money::to_tiyn_decimal` and `money::to_decimal` for `rust_decimal::Decimal` |

## Quick start

```rust,no_run
use tungo_sdk::Tungo;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> tungo_sdk::Result<()> {
    // The API key is read from TUNGO_API_KEY when it is not passed explicitly.
    let client = Tungo::builder()
        .company_id("co_01h455vb4pex5vsknk084sn02q")
        .build()?;

    let turn = client.ask("What is the VAT for October?").await?;
    println!("{}", turn.answer);
    println!("request id: {:?}", turn.request_id());
    Ok(())
}
```

## Authentication and configuration

Create one client and share it: it is immutable and safe to use from several threads or tasks. Every option can be passed explicitly; three of them fall back to environment variables.

| Option | Environment variable | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API key | `TUNGO_API_KEY` | none |
| Base URL | `TUNGO_BASE_URL` | `https://api.tungo.kz` |
| Webhook secret | `TUNGO_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | none |
| Default company and workspace | | none |
| Timeout | | 60 s (600 s for non-streaming chat turns) |
| Maximum retries | | 2 |
| Default headers, HTTP client | | none, built-in |

The API key is sent only to operations that require it; public endpoints and incoming hooks never receive it, and it never appears in error messages or debug output. Calling an authenticated operation without a key fails locally, before any request is made.

Every method also accepts per-request options: timeout, maximum retries, extra headers, an idempotency key and cancellation.

```rust,no_run
use std::time::Duration;

use tungo_sdk::{RequestOptions, Tungo};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> tungo_sdk::Result<()> {
    let client = Tungo::builder()
        .api_key("tg_...")
        .base_url("https://api.tungo.kz")
        .webhook_secret("whsec_...")
        .company_id("co_...")
        .workspace_id("ws_...")
        .timeout(Duration::from_secs(30))
        .max_retries(3)
        .default_header("x-client-name", "billing-service")
        // Your own reqwest settings (proxy, TLS, connection pool). The SDK
        // finishes the builder and turns redirects off, so the API key is
        // never forwarded to another host.
        .http_client_builder(tungo_sdk::reqwest::Client::builder())
        .build()?;

    // Per-request options: `with_options` returns a client that applies them
    // to every call made through it and shares the connection pool.
    let options = RequestOptions::new()
        .timeout(Duration::from_secs(5))
        .max_retries(0)
        .company_id("co_other")
        .header("x-trace-id", "trace-1")?;
    let company = client.with_options(options).companies().get().await?;

    // An idempotency key belongs to one request: the client returned by
    // `with_options` sends it once, with an operation that accepts it.
    let keyed = client.with_options(RequestOptions::new().idempotency_key("order-1532"));
    keyed.proposals().approve("P-000042", None).await?;

    // Every response carries its status, headers, request id and rate limit.
    println!("{} (HTTP {})", company.name, company.status());
    println!("request id: {:?}", company.request_id());
    println!("rate limit: {:?}", company.rate_limit());

    // Cancellation: drop the future, for example with a deadline of your own.
    let call = client.companies().list();
    if tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(1), call)
        .await
        .is_err()
    {
        println!("cancelled");
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

Company-scoped and workspace-scoped operations take the company and the workspace from the client (`company_id`, `workspace_id` on the builder) or from the request options, so they are not repeated in every call. `Tungo` is `Clone + Send + Sync`; its `Debug` output never contains the API key or the webhook secret, and `Debug` of `RequestOptions` prints header names without their values.

**Custom HTTP client.** Pass a `reqwest::ClientBuilder` to `http_client_builder`: the SDK turns redirects off before it builds the client, so the API key (a custom header that reqwest keeps across redirects) can never be forwarded to another host. If you pass a finished `reqwest::Client` to `http_client` instead, build it with `.redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::none())`; a response that still arrives from another origin fails with `Error::Config` and is discarded, and the key must then be treated as leaked.

**Idempotency keys.** An `idempotency_key` in the request options belongs to one request: the client returned by `with_options` sends it with the first operation that accepts an `Idempotency-Key` and refuses a second one with `Error::Validation`. Operations that do not accept the header (every `GET`) never carry it. Call `with_options` again to repeat a request with the same key.

**Decoding.** A field the contract requires must be present in a response: `{}` is an `Error::Decode`, not a model filled with zeros and empty strings. Optional fields are `Option`s. The optional parameters of an operation (`...Params`) are `#[non_exhaustive]`: build them with `Default::default()` or `new()` and the setter methods.

## Errors

Every failure is a subtype of the SDK's base error. An HTTP error response becomes an API error chosen by the `error.type` field of the response body, falling back to the HTTP status when the body is not the API's error envelope:

| `error.type` | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_request_error` | 400 |
| `authentication_error` | 401 |
| `payment_required_error` | 402 |
| `permission_error` | 403 |
| `not_found_error` | 404 |
| `conflict_error` | 409 |
| `gone_error` | 410 |
| `limit_error` | 429 |
| `api_error` | 500 |
| `unavailable_error` | 503 |

An API error carries the status, type, code, message, request id, field errors, the parsed retry-after delay, the response headers and the raw body. Problems that happen without a response have their own types: connection error, timeout, decode error (a successful response whose body is not valid), and configuration or validation error (raised before any request).

```rust,no_run
use tungo_sdk::{ApiErrorKind, Error, Tungo};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> tungo_sdk::Result<()> {
    let client = Tungo::from_env()?;

    match client.proposals().get("P-000042").await {
        Ok(proposal) => println!("{:?}", proposal.into_inner()),
        Err(Error::Api(error)) => {
            // status, type, code, message, request id, field errors, retry-after,
            // extra properties, headers and the raw body.
            eprintln!("{} {} {:?}", error.status, error.error_type, error.code);
            eprintln!("{} (request id {:?})", error.message, error.request_id);
            for field in &error.fields {
                eprintln!("  {}: {}", field.path, field.message);
            }
            match error.kind {
                ApiErrorKind::NotFound => eprintln!("no such proposal"),
                ApiErrorKind::Limit => eprintln!("retry after {:?}", error.retry_after),
                ApiErrorKind::Permission => {
                    eprintln!("missing {:?}", error.extra.get("permission"))
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Err(Error::Timeout { message, .. }) => eprintln!("timed out: {message}"),
        Err(Error::Connection { message, .. }) => eprintln!("network problem: {message}"),
        Err(Error::Decode { message, .. }) => eprintln!("unexpected response: {message}"),
        // Raised before any request: no API key, an empty identifier, ...
        Err(error @ (Error::Config(_) | Error::Validation(_))) => eprintln!("{error}"),
        Err(other) => return Err(other),
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

`Error` is a `#[non_exhaustive]` enum built with thiserror; the underlying transport or decoding error is available through `std::error::Error::source`. `Error::status()`, `Error::request_id()` and `Error::kind()` read the common fields without matching.

## Retries and timeouts

A request is retried up to 2 times (3 attempts) on connection errors, timeouts and the statuses 408, 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504, but only when repeating it is safe: `GET`, `HEAD`, `PUT` and `DELETE` requests, and `POST` or `PATCH` requests of the operations whose contract declares an `Idempotency-Key`. For those the SDK generates a random key and reuses it for every attempt; you can pass your own. Other operations send no key, not even one you pass, because the API would ignore it.

The delay between attempts is `min(0.5 s × 2^attempt, 8 s)` with random jitter. A positive `retry-after-ms` or `Retry-After` response header overrides it; if the server asks for more than 60 s the SDK does not wait and raises the error with the delay filled in.

The timeout covers the whole request including reading the body. Streaming calls have no total timeout, only a connect timeout and an idle timeout of 120 s. Cancellation supplied by the caller is combined with the timeout.

```rust,no_run
use std::time::Duration;

use tungo_sdk::{RequestOptions, Tungo};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> tungo_sdk::Result<()> {
    // For every call of this client: 5 retries, 20 s per attempt.
    let client = Tungo::builder()
        .max_retries(5)
        .timeout(Duration::from_secs(20))
        .build()?;

    // For one call: no retries, 2 s, and an idempotency key of your own.
    let options = RequestOptions::new()
        .max_retries(0)
        .timeout(Duration::from_secs(2))
        .idempotency_key("approve-P-000042");
    let decision = client
        .with_options(options)
        .proposals()
        .approve("P-000042", None)
        .await?;
    println!("{:?}", decision.into_inner());
    Ok(())
}
```

The policy itself is public in the `retry` module (`is_retryable_status`, `backoff_delay`, `parse_retry_after`). A `Retry-After` of zero or in the past does not make the SDK retry at once: the normal backoff applies.

## Pagination

List operations use cursor pagination (`{ data, next_cursor }`). The plain method returns one typed page that knows whether there is a next page and can fetch it. The auto-paging variant is a lazy iterator: it requests the next page only when needed, carries your filters over, and stops fetching as soon as you stop iterating.

```rust,no_run
use tungo_sdk::resources::ProposalsListParams;
use tungo_sdk::{TryStreamExt, Tungo};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> tungo_sdk::Result<()> {
    let client = Tungo::from_env()?;
    let params = ProposalsListParams::new().status("previewed").limit(50);

    // One page: the page model plus `has_next` and `next_page`.
    let page = client.proposals().list(&params).await?;
    println!("{} of {} proposals", page.data.len(), page.total);
    if let Some(next) = page.next_page().await? {
        println!("the next page has {} more", next.data.len());
    }

    // Every item: pages are requested lazily, with the same filters.
    let mut proposals = client.proposals().list_all(&params);
    while let Some(proposal) = proposals.try_next().await? {
        println!("{}", proposal.id);
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

`Page<P>` dereferences to the page model, so fields the API adds next to `data` (totals, counters) are read directly. If the server ever returns a cursor it has already returned (also in a longer cycle), the iteration stops with `Error::Pagination` instead of looping forever.

## Streaming

Streaming operations use server-sent events and deliver typed events as they arrive. Leaving the loop early or closing the stream closes the connection. A stream request is retried only before its first byte; an error response is raised as the same typed API error as for ordinary calls. A chat stream that ends before its final event is reported as an error, never as a finished answer.

```rust,no_run
use tungo_sdk::types::{ChatEvent, ChatMessageRequest};
use tungo_sdk::{StreamExt, Tungo};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> tungo_sdk::Result<()> {
    let client = Tungo::from_env()?;
    let request = ChatMessageRequest {
        message: Some("What is the VAT for October?".to_owned()),
        ..Default::default()
    };

    // Events arrive as the server sends them.
    let mut stream = client.chat().create_stream(&request).await?;
    println!(
        "dialog {:?}, turn {:?}",
        stream.dialog_id(),
        stream.turn_no()
    );
    while let Some(event) = stream.next().await {
        match event? {
            ChatEvent::Text(text) => print!("{}", text.delta),
            ChatEvent::Tool(tool) => eprintln!("[{} {}]", tool.name, tool.status),
            ChatEvent::Error(error) => eprintln!("error: {}", error.error.message),
            ChatEvent::Done(done) => eprintln!("\nstop reason: {:?}", done.stop_reason),
            _ => {}
        }
    }

    // Or let the SDK fold the stream into the final answer. An `error` event
    // is returned as `Error::Stream`, and a stream that ends before its
    // `done` event as `Error::Decode`: a partial text is never the answer.
    let turn = client
        .ask_stream("And for November?")
        .await?
        .accumulate()
        .await?;
    println!("{} (cost: {:?} tiyn)", turn.text, turn.cost_tiyn);
    Ok(())
}
```

`chat().list_events`, `feed().list_events` and `batches().list_events` return the same kind of stream. Heart-beats are skipped; `into_raw()` gives the raw server-sent events. A stream has no total timeout: it fails with `Error::Timeout` when no bytes arrive for 120 s (`stream_idle_timeout` on the builder or in the request options). An event type this version does not know arrives as `ChatEvent::Unknown` with its raw JSON, and so does an event that lacks a property its type requires. `accumulate()` fails with `Error::Decode` when the stream ends before its `done` event (a partial text is never returned as the answer) and skips an event it cannot decode (`ChatTurn::skipped_events`). A successful response that is not `text/event-stream` is an `Error::Decode` as well. The exception is a finished chat turn that the API replays for a repeated `Idempotency-Key` (`application/json` with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`): its stored result arrives as the events of that turn, ending with `next` (follow-ups and the next action, when it has them) and `done`.

## Webhooks

Outgoing webhooks are signed according to the Standard Webhooks specification (Svix). The verify helper takes the raw request body and the headers (`webhook-*` or `svix-*`), checks the HMAC-SHA256 signature in constant time and the timestamp within 300 s of the system clock, and returns the typed event. Any problem is reported as a webhook verification error. If no secret is passed, the client's webhook secret is used.

The send-hook helper posts an event to an incoming hook (`/hooks/{token}`) and, when given a secret, signs the exact bytes it sends in the `X-Signature: sha256=<hex>` header. The API key is never sent to hooks.

```rust,no_run
use tungo_sdk::types::WebhookEvent;
use tungo_sdk::{HookPayload, Tungo};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> tungo_sdk::Result<()> {
    // The webhook secret is read from TUNGO_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
    let client = Tungo::from_env()?;

    // In your HTTP handler: the raw body and the request headers. Any
    // `http::HeaderMap`, string map or slice of pairs works as headers.
    let body = br#"{"id":"evt_1","type":"ping","created_at":"2026-11-09T15:00:00Z"}"#;
    let headers = [
        ("webhook-id", "msg_2xyzExample123"),
        ("webhook-timestamp", "1793974568"),
        (
            "webhook-signature",
            "v1,4H/XE/Z5TVdWNr7mzvFh+DuOghc+OuBDkZ1b82Fwhww=",
        ),
    ];
    match client.verify_webhook(body, &headers) {
        Ok(WebhookEvent::ProposalWritten(event)) => println!("written: {:?}", event.data),
        Ok(event) => println!("event {:?}", event.tag()),
        Err(error) => eprintln!("rejected ({}): {error}", error.reason()),
    }

    // Send an event to an incoming hook, signed with the hook's secret.
    let payload = HookPayload::bytes(
        r#"{"id":"order_1532","amount_tiyn":4500000}"#,
        "application/json",
    )
    .secret("hksec_...")
    .event_id("order_1532");
    let accepted = client.send_hook("hk_token", payload).await?;
    println!("runs started: {:?}", accepted.run_ids);
    Ok(())
}
```

`webhooks::WebhookVerifier` verifies with an explicit secret, a custom tolerance or a fixed clock (for tests); `webhooks::verify_hook_signature` checks the `X-Signature` of an incoming hook on the receiving side. `client.automations().post_hook(token, payload)` is the same call as `client.send_hook(token, payload)`.

## Money

The API expresses amounts in tiyn (1/100 of a tenge) as 64-bit integers. The money helper converts decimal strings and exact decimal values to tiyn without floating-point error, rounding half away from zero (`"1.005"` → `101`), and formats tiyn for display (`4500000` → `45 000,00 ₸`). Invalid input raises a typed error.

```rust,no_run
use tungo_sdk::money::{format_tiyn, format_tiyn_in, is_valid_bin_iin, to_tiyn, to_tiyn_f64};

fn main() -> Result<(), tungo_sdk::MoneyError> {
    // Decimal strings are converted exactly, rounding half away from zero.
    let tiyn = to_tiyn("45000.50")?;
    assert_eq!(tiyn, 4_500_050);
    assert_eq!(to_tiyn("1.005")?, 101);
    assert!(to_tiyn("1,5").is_err());

    // A float goes through its shortest decimal form; prefer strings.
    assert_eq!(to_tiyn_f64(1.005)?, 101);
    assert!(to_tiyn_f64(f64::NAN).is_err());

    assert_eq!(format_tiyn(tiyn), "45 000,50 ₸");
    assert_eq!(format_tiyn_in(123_456, "USD"), "1 234,56 $");
    assert!(is_valid_bin_iin("990140000017"));
    println!("{}", format_tiyn(tiyn));
    Ok(())
}
```

`TungoMoney` offers the same functions as associated functions, under the name the other Tungo SDKs use.

## Long-running operations

`wait_for_run`, `run_scenario_and_wait` and `wait_for_batch` poll until the run or the batch reaches a final state. The interval starts at 1 s and grows to 5 s; when the deadline (10 minutes by default) passes first, they fail with `Error::Timeout`. A state this version does not know is polled again; an answer without the state (or, for a batch, without its `running` flag) is an `Error::Decode`, never a finished job. Dropping the future cancels the wait.

```rust,no_run
use std::time::Duration;

use tungo_sdk::{Tungo, WaitOptions};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> tungo_sdk::Result<()> {
    let client = Tungo::from_env()?;
    let options = WaitOptions::new().timeout(Duration::from_secs(120));
    let run = client.run_scenario_and_wait("sc_...", None, &options).await?;
    println!("{}: {:?}", run.state, run.answer);
    Ok(())
}
```

## API reference

Generated from the Tungo Platform API contract: **13 resources, 85 methods, 22 webhook event types**.

| Resource | Description | Methods |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `client.workspaces()` | Organisations (workspaces) the API key can access | `list` |
| `client.companies()` | Companies of an organisation and their profiles | `list` · `get` |
| `client.platform()` | Platform balance, ledger, usage reports, limits, audit log and model rates | `list_usage_rates` · `get_account` · `get_audit / get_audit_all` · `get_ledger / get_ledger_all` · `list_limits` · `list_requests / list_requests_all` · `get_usage` |
| `client.api_keys()` | The current API key and its usage statistics | `get_current` · `get_current_usage` · `get_usage` |
| `client.webhooks()` | Outgoing webhooks of an organisation (Svix): endpoints, event catalogue, deliveries and signature check | `list_endpoints / list_endpoints_all` · `create_endpoint` · `get_endpoint` · `update_endpoint` · `delete_endpoint` · `list_endpoint_attempts / list_endpoint_attempts_all` · `rotate_endpoint_secret` · `test_endpoint` · `list_event_types` · `list_messages / list_messages_all` · `list_message_attempts / list_message_attempts_all` · `resend_message` · `get_usage` |
| `client.chat()` | Conversations with the AI accountant: questions, streaming chat (SSE), token counting and history | `list / list_all` · `create / create_stream` · `count_tokens` · `list_mentions` · `list_suggestions` · `get` · `update` · `delete` · `answer / answer_stream` · `list_events` · `stop` |
| `client.proposals()` | Documents proposed by the AI accountant: review, approval for posting to 1C, and rejection | `list / list_all` · `approve_batch` · `get` · `approve` · `reject` · `request_approval` |
| `client.feed()` | The company's feed of events and proposals (pages and a live SSE stream) | `get / get_all` · `list_events` |
| `client.batches()` | Processing batches for bank statements, incoming e-invoices and DirectBank | `list / list_all` · `create_bank_statement` · `create_esf_purchases` · `get` · `list_events` · `stop` · `get_summary` · `list_statements / list_statements_all` · `poll_directbank` |
| `client.esf()` | Incoming and outgoing electronic invoices (the ESF system) | `get_incoming / get_incoming_all` · `get_outgoing / get_outgoing_all` |
| `client.forms()` | Tax forms (FNO 100.00 and others): building, ISNA checks and data gaps | `list` · `build` · `list_data_gaps` · `get_isna` · `list_notes` |
| `client.onec()` | Status of the company's connection to its 1C database | `get_status` |
| `client.automations()` | Company automations: incoming hooks, scenarios, step chains, runs and the AI autonomy level | `post_hook` · `list_hooks` · `create_hook` · `get_hook` · `update_hook` · `delete_hook` · `rotate_hook` · `test_hook` · `list_runs / list_runs_all` · `get_run` · `cancel_run` · `retry_run` · `list_scenarios` · `create_scenario` · `get_scenario` · `put_scenario` · `update_scenario` · `delete_scenario` · `run_scenario` · `get_state` · `put_state` · `get_autonomy` · `put_autonomy` |

The same API is available in ten languages. All SDKs are generated from one contract and behave the same way.

| Language | Repository | Package |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TypeScript | [tungo-sdk-typescript](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-typescript) | `@tungoai/sdk` |
| Python | [tungo-sdk-python](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-python) | `tungoai` |
| Go | [tungo-sdk-go](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-go) | `github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-go` |
| **Rust** | [tungo-sdk-rust](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-rust) | `tungo-sdk` |
| PHP | [tungo-sdk-php](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-php) | `tungo/sdk` |

## Versioning and support

This library follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/). While the major version is 0, a minor release may contain breaking changes; they are always listed in the [changelog](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-rust/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). This README describes version 0.3.0.

The code is generated: please report problems and ideas in the [issue tracker](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-rust/issues) rather than opening pull requests against generated files. To report a vulnerability, follow the [security policy](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-rust/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
